chunks: One of our companions, his chain having dropped from me, narrated from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not leave out anything that is needed except that He taught it to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So, from His teaching him was that he ascended the pulpit one day, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'O people! Jibraeel came to me from the Subtle, the All-Knowing, and said: 'The virgins are like fruit on a tree. When the fruit ripens and is not picked, the sun spoils it and the winds scatter it. And so are the virgins when they reach what women reach; there is no cure for them except the husband, otherwise there is no safety for them from corruption, for they are human beings.'

He said: So a man stood up to him and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, whom should we marry them to?' He said, 'Their matches.' He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, and who are their matches?' He said, 'The believers are matches for one another. The believers are matches for one another.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling regarding the marriage of virgins according to the Prophet's teaching in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophetic wisdom regarding the natural physiological needs of women, using the metaphor of unharvested fruit to emphasize that marriage is the divinely prescribed remedy to prevent moral corruption. It establishes the principle of 'kafa'ah' (compatibility), defining it broadly as shared faith, which underscores the spiritual equality of believers in marital selection within Shia jurisprudence.
